answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy grows identity on a reputation trellis: each new agent needs vouching from bonded peers, and every vouch locks a slice of the guarantor's stake, so trust is scarce and traceable. Reputation forms like jade, slow and expensive to counterfeit. When fake agents flood in, the graph tightens into a spiral of escalating proofs: each newcomer must post stake, pass peer attestation and survive a cooldown before earning. An attacker's cost then scales with every clone it spawns, making mass identity unprofitable.
